subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: Should gateway stop/restart boundedly cancel active/background exec child processes, or preserve current background/yielded exec semantics and only improve diagnostics/recovery?
rationale: The source shows both a real shutdown availability problem and intentional background exec preservation; changing that behavior affects running user work and needs maintainer policy before implementation.

options.title: Bounded shutdown cancellation
options.body: Cancel and await process-supervisor exec children during gateway stop/restart within the existing shutdown budget while keeping normal agent-turn abort behavior unchanged.

options.title: Preserve background exec
options.body: Keep background/yielded exec processes alive across shutdown attempts and add stronger diagnostics plus operator recovery guidance instead of killing work automatically.

options.title: Defer to session kill design
options.body: Keep this issue open but make the broader session/process ownership decision in the related session-kill work before changing gateway shutdown behavior.

recommendation.title: Bounded shutdown cancellation
recommendation.body: Cancel and await process-supervisor exec children during gateway stop/restart within the existing shutdown budget while keeping normal agent-turn abort behavior unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway lifecycle and shutdown history makes this the best available owner for the policy choice.
